name: AG Lit Sisters Presents: Beyond The Ballot - Thematic Book Club
description:
What does it mean to be a woman in politics? To lead, negotiate, dissent, survive and make decisions in a world where power has never been equally distributed?
This November, AG Lit Sisters turns its attention to women in politics, their journeys, struggles, ambitions and legacies.
Inspired by the forthcoming book The Belonging by Sonia Gandhi, releasing on 10 November, this gathering is an invitation to look beyond political headlines and electoral victories. We want to explore the women behind the public personas: their choices, convictions, contradictions and the histories they have shaped.
From Indira Gandhi to contemporary political leaders, from parliamentarians to grassroots movements, whose stories have we heard, and whose voices remain missing?
Bring a book, an opinion, and your curiosity. You don't have to agree with everyone. You only have to be willing to have a conversation.
📚 AG Lit Sisters | November Edition
📅 Sunday, 22 November 2026
⏰ 11 AM to 1 PM
📍 Atta Galatta, Indiranagar, Bengaluru
Readers are welcome, but non-readers are celebrated.

name: Give me your best offer - Turn your product into an offer people will buy
description:
If you’ve got a great business idea or you've recently launched but you're wondering why the sales aren't coming in, this one's for you.
Often many new founders realise too late that building a great product and knowing how to sell it are two very different things.
The difference? A compelling OFFER.
One that speaks to the right customer, solves a real need, communicates your value and gives people a reason to choose YOU.
That's exactly what we'll work on in this hands-on workshop led by brand communications specialist Barira Nabeel and hosted by Sudhir Kiran of First Brick Collective.
You'll learn how to:

Identify who your customer really is
Understand what makes them buy
Discover what sets your product apart
Package and position your offer
Build and pitch your OWN offer, right there in the room

Join us in a relaxed, informal setting and take away practical tools and fresh perspectives on YOUR business.
You've built the product. Now give people a reason to buy it

name: Watercolour Florals - Watercolour Workshop
description:
Join us at Atta Galatta for a hands-on watercolour workshop exploring the beauty of loose, flowy floral painting.  
We'll begin with a few warm-up exercises to get comfortable with handling the brush, water and pigments. Gradually, we'll move on to painting leaves and petals, learning simple brush techniques to create different flower shapes before putting these elements together to paint a colourful bunch of flowers.  
You can take home all your finished paintings and practice sheets.  No prior experience is required. All painting materials will be provided, so just come ready to learn, experiment and enjoy painting!

name: The Gathering Room - Still Their Parent - Support Group
description:
You’ve been holding it together for them. Come and be held, for a change
Separation ends a marriage. It doesn’t end parenting.
Whether you’re raising your children on your own, sharing them with someone you can barely speak to, or living apart from them, you’re still showing up. For the school forms and the pick-ups. The questions you don’t know how to answer. The grandparents who miss them. The relatives with opinions on how you’re doing it.
Somewhere in all of it, a story tends to settle in: that you’ve failed them, that they’ll carry this forever, that you’re not allowed to fall apart. This session starts from a different premise: a parent who is struggling is still a parent who is trying, and the one holding everything together needs holding too.
This is for any parent navigating separation, whether you’re in the thick of it, past it, or still finding your feet.
The Format
This isn’t parenting advice, a talk, or a lecture, and no one here will tell you what’s best for your children. Expect movement, a few structured group activities done in pairs or as a full group, and space throughout to simply notice where you are. No performance or scripts. You’ve nothing to prepare.
What to Expect
Arrival
Come as you are. No small talk required, and nothing you owe anyone an explanation for.
In the room
For once, you won’t be the only parent who has been through this, or is going through it right now. No agenda beyond arriving, connecting, being present, and seeing what surfaces.
Leaving
You may leave with more clarity. You may leave having said nothing at all and still feel less alone. Both are the point.
Our Promise
What’s shared here stays here. You choose what to share, and you’re never asked to name or describe your ex or anyone else.
This is an ongoing gathering, held at regular intervals. Whether this is your first time in the room or you’ve been here before, you’re welcome. Seats need to be booked in advance.

name: Mycelium & Muse - A Science Storytelling Workshop
description:
We often equate creativity with making art. Picasso was creative. Beethoven was creative. Van Gogh was creative. But what about the person who first picked up a piece of charcoal and scribbled on the wall of a cave, hoping the people in the next cave would get  the message? Or the bowerbird who spends an entire season collecting blue bottle caps and flowers to decorate a little stage for a Mate? And what about a fungus? This one is literally brainless, yet it sends out electrical signals that, when connected to a synthesiser, play out like music. So if creativity shows up in organisms without brains, it is far older than us, isn't it?
That's the question we'll sit with: 
Where does creativity really begin on the tree of life, and what does that mean for all of us who have spent years saying "I'm just not the creative type". Along the way, you'll hear a mushroom playing music, make an idea card that is deliberately, wonderfully bad, write a letter to your future self, and discover a new answer to the question “Am I creative?” You don't need any science background to join in. Just come in, and let's get some creativity
Brewing. Because, tell you what, we are not sure if a creative life is a happier one. But we can absolutely guarantee that it's a far more meaningful one.
 
About the facilitator: 
Bitasta Datta is a microbiologist by training, an educator by profession and a science storyteller by passion.
For over 10 years, she has been turning science into stories for school learners and curious adults. She started at the National Digital Library of India, went on to co-found The Synapse, led curriculum and learning experience design at BYJU'S and Tutopiya, and now leads the efforts at Khan Academy India to narrate science in a way that sticks.
She believes science and art are two lenses on the same world, and that if you look through both long enough, you arrive at the same philosophy. So that's what she does. She dissects science to find the art in it, dissects art to find the science in it, and narrates her findings as stories.
Outside work, she paints, bakes, and travels, and writes about the places where science, art and philosophy run into each other. Mycelium & Muse began as one of those pieces

name: Demystifying the P word - Poetry Workshop
description:
Do you find poetry inaccessible, opaque, difficult to read and appreciate?
As the oldest form of literature, right from the oral tradition, poetry has always been the way humans told their stories. From Gilgamesh to Homer, from Kalidasa to Wordsworth, from Neruda to Akhmatova, poetry has brought us tales of love and loss and beauty and war.
If you want to explore poetry, learn ways to break it down, understand its nuances, its special code, its peculiar love language, then join us as we run you through a selection of poems that let you develop a set of hacks that you can employ when you read your next poem.
Whether you are just curious, a poetry enthusiast still trying to figure it out, or a poet hoping to expand your writing horizon, there is something here for you to listen to, learn from, and laugh with. Come, hear the stories behind the poems and the poems behind the stories.  
About Alt Poetry:
Alt Poetry is a multi-channel poetry platform that brings poets, readers, and poetry lovers together to read, discover, and debate poetry from all around the world. We host different events online and in-person, including ‘Poet of the Month’, ‘Book Talk’, ‘Poetry Atlas ’, and ‘Poetry Classroom’.
Alt Poetry is founded by Namratha Varadharajan (Author: On Cultivating Loudspeakers and Quilts -forthcoming from Booksthakam), Madhuri Katti (Author: Life, Time, and Other Things), and Rajani Radhakrishnan (Author: Water to Water, Duplicity, and No Way Home)
Limited spots available.

name: The Imitation Englishman  - Book launch
description:
What do family stories leave behind, and where does history end and fiction begin?
In 1916, a young man travelled from Almora to Heidelberg to study law. Along the way, someone stole his shoes. This unlikely episode from Devki Pande's family history became the starting point for The Imitation Englishman, a novel that takes us into a fascinating, yet lesser-known chapter of Indian history.
At the launch of her book, Devki will be in conversation with Ponnu Elizabeth Mathew, author of The Remnants of Rebellion, another novel inspired by an incident from her family history.
Join them for a conversation about the stories we inherit, the histories we uncover and the journey to fiction.

name: Crochet Workshop - Art Workshop
description:
Been wanting to crochet? Or just looking for another cute little hobby to obsess over? 👀🧶
Well, it's time to get your hands tangled in some yarn!
Join us for an evening of learning the basics of crochet and turning little loops of yarn into the cutest keychains.
You'll learn how to hold your hook, try basic stitches and make your very own crochet creation to take home!
No experience, no skills, no pressure. Just show up, get a little crafty and prepare to say, "Wait, I MADE THIS?!" 🥹
All materials are on us. Just bring yourself and your enthusiasm!

name: Decluttering & Fashion Rituals - Reading Circle
description:
You open a packed wardrobe and think, “I have nothing to wear.” Most of us treat fashion decluttering as a weekend chore: toss a few old clothes and accessories (material objects), clear a shelf, move on. But what we hold on to, and what we let go of, often says more about where we are in life than we’d admit.
Atta Galatta is hosting a reading and conversation around Bhawana Pingali’s The Art of Decluttering: Ancient Practices for Modern Living. There are no minimalist or maximalist rules and no styling tips. Instead, the evening is built around sthiram (or sthirata), the Sanskrit idea of steadiness, and the tweaked old Indian rituals Bhawana writes about in her book, which can make getting dressed feel like less of a chore.
Bhawana will read a few passages, take questions, and talk with the room about how clothes, body, mind, home, and identity shape our days. If you want to buy less and use more, are going through a change in your life, or simply like talking about fashion and books, you’re welcome to join.
About the Host
Bhawana Pingali is the author of The Art of Decluttering: Ancient Practices for Modern Living and the founder of Revastra, a storytelling platform that applies ancient Indian practices to how we care for our bodies, minds, and wardrobes. She is a fashion writer, researcher, and yoga-meditation facilitator whose work focuses on slow fashion and textile care. She also teaches writing on design and fashion communication as adjunct faculty at NIFT, Pearl Academy, Symbiosis, and IIM Ahmedabad. Her work encourages people to buy less on impulse and to see their clothes as a record of memory and identity.

name: The Pranic Advantage. Leaping Towards The Greatest Career Possibilities, Success & Impact - Pranic Healing Session
description:
Pranic Healing is a revolutionary no-touch, no-drug tested energy-based treatment that uses Prana, Chi or Energy to improve a wide range of physical, psychological, relationship, and financial issues.  Learn About The Power Of Pranic Self-healing for Professionals & Businesses. Achieve Personal & Professional (All-Round) Success & Fulfillment.
Questions & Answers: 1 Live Healing Demo
Speaker: Shravya Gubbi (Pranic Healer, 2X Entrepreneur)
Organiser: Pranic Healing for Free & Abundant Living

name: Lino Print Workshop - Art Workshop
description:
This hands-on workshop introduces the basics of lino cut printmaking, from carving a simple design to inking and printing your own artwork. Participants will be guided through the process step by step and will leave with their own prints, perfect as small artworks or gifts.
The session runs for three hours and includes demonstrations, supported making time, and space to experiment.
Open to beginners and anyone curious about printmaking — no prior experience needed. Suitable for ages 14+.
What should I bring?
Clothes you don’t mind getting messy in, ideas or finished sketches for designs (found images from books are welcome), and lots of creativity.
What’s provided?
All printing tools, paper, and inks will be provided.
What do I take home?
All finished artworks are yours to keep, along with any unfinished pieces. Participants will also keep their carved lino block, allowing them to reprint at home with basic supplies.
What's included:

Lino sheet
Lino carving tool
Lino ink
140gsm paper
Baren
Roller

name: Bella & Rami  - Book launch
description:
Join us at Atta Galatta for the book launch of “Bella & Rami”
 
About the Book: 
Bangalore, 1980. An Australian girl and an Indian boy fall in love at first sight. Decades of distance, loss, and hardship follow, yet their love endures. Bella & Rami is an unconventional romance based on a true story, told through scenes, letters, and poems.
 
About the Author:
Isobel de Border is an Australian author whose deep, lifelong connection to India shapes her narrative landscape. Her debut autofiction novel, Bella & Rami, draws extensively on real-world cross-continental correspondence, diaries, and archives spanning from 1980s Bangalore to contemporary Australia. Moving between both 
MEDIA KIT: ISOBEL DE BORDER AUTHOR
countries, her work explores the complex emotional geography of intimate relationships, and the interplay of time, distance and memory. De Border’s debut novel Bella & Rami is published in India by Timeless Script House, and internationally by Atmosphere Press, USA. De Border lives in Naarm, Melbourne, Australia
About the Host:
Asha Seth is an author, poet, former advertising Creative Director and the founder of MissBookThief, an award-winning literary platform that began as a book blog in 2012 and evolved into a book marketing agency working with authors and publishers.

name: Chouboli - Storytelling performance
description:
What if a centuries-old folktale could speak to the modern world? 
Chouboli is a storytelling performance in Hindi, adapted from the renowned author Vijaydan Detha's biting satire in Rajasthani.  
Funny, philosophical and a little wild, It weaves ethical dilemmas and lyrical riddles into a story-within-a-story that is part fantasy, part mirror.
A beautiful mess of being human, presented with sharp wit and seamless flow between fantasy and realism, magic and logic, fact and fiction!  
90 minutes. Entirely alive!
Language : Hindi  
Adaptation & performance by Narendra Shekhawat

name: Divine Delicacies - Storytelling and Menu Tasting Session
description:
Where food meets faith, and every prasadam has a story!
Can you imagine worship without food? From festival feasts to little-known prasadams and fascinating rituals, food has always been an essential part of our connection with the divine.
Join Aparna Jaishankar for a deliciously different storytelling experience! Come taste samples of home-made temple offerings while discovering the stories behind them. A bit of history, mythology, philosophy, politics all served for the divine palate! Come hungry. Come curious. Leave with a whole new appetite for stories!

name: A Little Book of Light - Book lamp-making workshop
description:
A few blank pages, a little folding, a little imagination… and a touch of light!  
What if a book could glow?  
Come spend a cosy afternoon folding, shaping, and bringing pages together to create your very own little book lamp.  
Where origami meets bookmaking, ordinary paper takes on a whole new form — a sculptural creation that glows with a warm, gentle light.  
No experience needed. Just bring your curiosity and a little love for making things by hand.  
We'll bring all the materials. You bring yourself!  
Fold · Create · Illuminate

name: The Fearless Four - Book launch
description:
Join us at Atta Galatta for the book launch of “The Fearless Four”
Who says mystery is only for grown-ups? Meet Meenu, Damayanthi, Avisu, and Zara – four brave best friends who call themselves ‘The Fearless Four’. The Fearless Four part 2 - The paper's, the phrase and the chase is a sequel to the Fearless Four part 1. It is about question papers for a national level exam which mysteriously disappear and the Fearless Four have to solve the mystery.
About the Author: Avya Krishna is a student of Grade 6 at Baldwin Girls High School, Bangalore. She is learning the piano, Bharatanatyam, and is also a medal 
winner in swimming. She is an avid reader. Right from the tender age of three, she was always found with a book in hand. Trekking and adventures excite her, and she is been on a couple of camps and treks with her family. Inspired by her parents who have also authored books, she took a keen interest in writing. 
She was also awarded by the District Governor of Rotary Club, Chennai for her exemplary performance.  
As a part of this launch, she would be planning an engaging session with kids aged 4 plus and their parents

Time: 4 pm- 6 pm 
Venue: Atta Galatta, Indiranagar

name: Conversations and practices for pleasure, presence, and connection - Panel Discussion and Workshop
description:
PANEL DISCUSSION | Beyond the Hands
Conversations about sex work often centre a female-centred story. Male and trans sex workers speak about visibility, representation, and being left out of the dominant narrative.
WORKSHOP | Sensual Play: Sensuality Is a Practice
Why can touch feel electric with one person and disconnected with another? This consent-forward workshop explores sensuality as attention, not just technique. Through somatic exercises, solo and partnered practice, and a look at how the nervous system processes touch, safety, and arousal, you'll release performance anxiety and return to genuine feeling.

name: ಒಂದು ವಲಸೆ ಕಥೆ - Book launch
description: On 6 December 2026, from 11 am to 1 pm, join Indian-American traveler, poet, and novelist Kiran Bhat as he launches his first Kannada-language poetry book, ಒಂದು ವಲಸೆ ಕಥೆ. Bhat will discuss how he writes poetry in different languages and his experiences living in various countries. The event will be guided by fellow poet Dadapeer Jyman.

name: Room on the Roof - Book launch
description: Illustrator Saumya Oberoi is thrilled to welcome you to the book launch of The Room on the Roof: A Graphic Novel, a special adaptation of Ruskin Bond's classic first novel. This book tells the coming-of-age story of Rusty afresh as he runs away from his strict English guardian’s house to rent a room on the roof in post-Independence Dehradun. Along the way, he discovers a world of true friendship, innocent first love, and a profound understanding of the self. Learn about the process behind the 125-page full-color book and enjoy an evening of chatting about graphic narratives, storytelling for young adults, and the importance of chaat!

name: Submergence - Book Signing
description:
Join us at Atta Galatta for a special book signing with Anjali M S, a young, up-and-coming author who is about to release her YA dystopian book Submergence. Submergence is a dystopian novel set in a future where wars, pollution, and a catastrophic asteroid impact have submerged nearly all of Earth, leaving behind one continent divided between two rival governments. While one fights to restore the dying planet, the other looks to space travel for humanity’s salvation. Caught between these opposing ideologies are a spy and a murderous soldier whose fates are dangerously intertwined.
Come meet Anjali, discover her work, and get your copy signed. Whether you're an enthusiastic reader, an aspiring writer, or simply someone who loves a good story, this is an opportunity to connect with a young author and celebrate the joy of books.


Date: 23 January 2027


Time: 2:00–3:00 PM


Venue: Atta Galatta, Bengaluru


Instagram handle: @anjalims_author


Format: Author meet-and-greet and book signing


Age Group: 12+ 


We look forward to welcoming readers for an afternoon celebrating books, storytelling, and the next generation of authors.
